# Live paper fixtures

Run `python3 scripts/generate_live_paper_template.py` from the repository root to
rebuild the synthetic images and bundled printable PDF. Development dependencies:
ReportLab, NumPy and OpenCV Python with ArUco support. The application does not use
Python or OpenCV for live recognition.

All physical dimensions in these fixtures are **synthetic test scale**. They do
not establish printer accuracy, camera metrology, or accuracy on a physical page.

Three A4 templates contain 16 mm ArUco `DICT_4X4_50` markers, with distinct
identifier sets: FRONT uses IDs 0 through 3, TOP uses 4 through 7, SIDE uses
8 through 11. The identifiers establish the sketch view as well as corner order.
Show one complete template at a time. A missing marker pauses recognition;
multiple complete templates are ambiguous and also pause recognition.

Each view uses the same physical layout. Markers, in ascending ID order, are
centered at `(17, 30)`, `(193, 30)`, `(193, 266)`, `(17, 266)` mm measured from
the sheet's top-left. The drawing region spans `(25, 38)` through `(185, 258)` mm.
Sketch coordinates use the drawing region's bottom-left as origin. Print at
actual size and check the separate 50 mm footer segment with a ruler.

- `blank.png`: four markers with an empty drawing region.
- `primitives.png`: line from `(15, 180)` to `(85, 180)` mm; rectangle spanning
  `(15, 120)` to `(85, 160)` mm; circle centered at `(115, 140)` mm with 12 mm
  radius; point at `(115, 185)` mm. Stroke width and round caps are finite.
- `primitives-top.png` and `primitives-side.png`: identical known drawing
  geometry, with their respective perimeter marker IDs and visible view label.
  The view labels remain outside the drawing region.
- `perspective-noise.png`: independently projected `primitives.png` with seeded
  additive pixel noise.
- `junctions.png`: T and X junctions plus a broken straight stroke requiring
  confirmation; joining intent cannot be inferred from those pixels alone.
- `marker-loss.png`: one obscured marker; recognition pauses.
- `occlusion.png`: an opaque ellipse covers drawing geometry while preserving
  marker visibility; accepted geometry remains owned by the live session.

Marker patterns are generated with OpenCV's standard dictionary. Fixture geometry
and image transformations are generated by this repository. The bundled PDFs use vector marker cells, an empty drawing region, a large
FRONT/TOP/SIDE header, print instructions and a scale check. Assets are
`live-paper-template.pdf` (FRONT), `live-paper-template-top.pdf` and
`live-paper-template-side.pdf` under `src-tauri/assets/`. The vendored skeleton implementation and its MIT license reside in
`src-tauri/src/services/vendor/`.
